h1: The Quarter Onnut by UHG — 4-Star Rooftop Pool in Bangkok's Relaxed On Nut-Phra Khanong Neighbourhood
intro: If you want a 4-star hotel on Bangkok's Sukhumvit strip without paying central-district prices, The Quarter Onnut by UHG is a name that keeps coming up among guests who know the area well. Sitting at the mouth of Sukhumvit Soi 58 inside the Sukhumvit Hills development in Phra Khanong, this hotel opened in 2021 with 88 rooms, a rooftop outdoor pool with proper Bangkok skyline views, a modern gym, and a restaurant serving buffet breakfast. It sits roughly midway between BTS On Nut and BTS Bang Chak — about a 10-minute walk to either. Rates start from approximately ฿1,200/night, with a score of 8.6 from 403 reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: The Quarter Onnut by UHG is the hotel component of the Sukhumvit Hills mixed-use development that launched in 2021. The project brought a fresh 4-star property to a corner of Sukhumvit that's long been favoured by Bangkok expats and younger travellers who want access to the city's BTS network without paying the premium of Thonglor or Asok. Phra Khanong is genuinely local — lower prices, street food a few steps away, and a real neighbourhood feel that fades somewhere around Sukhumvit 40 heading inward.

The 88 rooms span four categories: Superior Twin and Superior King (21–27 sqm), the standard entry-level options; Deluxe Room (35 sqm), a noticeably more comfortable step up; and a Family Suite with two bedrooms for groups or families. All rooms include minibar, in-room safe, air conditioning, Smart TV, and complimentary Wi-Fi. The interior fit-out is clean and contemporary — no heritage character, no gimmicks — but the build quality is what you'd hope for from a 2021 opening.
"Rooftop pool with a great city view. Room spotless, staff genuinely helpful. For this price in On Nut you're not going to find a 4-star with a rooftop pool like this anywhere else."

The rooftop outdoor pool is the property's headline feature, and guest reviews back it up. The Bangkok skyline view is unobstructed — good at sunset, dramatic at night. The fitness centre on the same level uses up-to-date equipment, a benefit of the hotel being newly built rather than renovated. The hotel's restaurant opens daily for a buffet breakfast offering Thai, Chinese, and American selections at an additional ฿209 per adult (children under six free).

The On Nut–Phra Khanong neighbourhood brings its own appeal as well. W District, the outdoor bar and street food complex that draws Bangkok's night-out crowd, is a short Grab ride away. Habito Mall and Summer Hill — two of the city's most popular hangout spots for independent cafes and weekend brunches — are nearby. The Big C on On Nut road covers supermarket needs. For shopping or nightlife that requires the full Sukhumvit experience, the BTS ride from On Nut to Siam takes under 20 minutes.

What to know going in: several reviews flag noise from the BTS elevated track and Sukhumvit Road, particularly in rooms facing the main road. It's the kind of ambient city noise that doesn't bother most urban travellers but can disturb light sleepers — request an inner-facing or soi-facing room when checking in. Some reviews also mention inconsistent hot water pressure during peak evening hours, and the 760-metre walk to BTS On Nut — comfortable in good weather, a slight inconvenience if it's raining without a Grab in sight.

The overall picture from real guest reviews is positive: The Quarter Onnut by UHG delivers value that's hard to match at the 4-star level in this neighbourhood. A rooftop pool, proper gym, good service, and a 2021 build quality — all at rates that sit well below comparable properties in Thonglor or Asok. TripAdvisor ranks it #113 of 1,384 Bangkok hotels, which for a three-year-old property in a quieter district is a genuine achievement.

honestSummary: The Quarter Onnut by UHG delivers above its price point for 4-star accommodation in Bangkok's On Nut–Phra Khanong corridor — rooftop pool, modern gym, good service, fresh 2021 build. The caveats are real but minor: rooms aren't large, some road noise is present in outward-facing rooms, and the BTS walk is 10 minutes rather than door-to-door.
honestChecks: If you need large rooms or a bathtub — Superior rooms run 21–27 sqm, which is compact → consider the Deluxe Room (35 sqm) or Family Suite if space matters to you
If you're a light sleeper — road-facing rooms can be noisy from the BTS and Sukhumvit traffic → request an inner/soi-facing room at check-in

If you need direct covered BTS access — the 760m walk to On Nut is pleasant in fine weather but requires a Grab in the rain → Cross Vibe Bangkok Sukhumvit (200m to BTS) is the better pick if station-proximity is your priority

tips.title: Best pool time: late afternoon
tips.body: The Bangkok skyline looks best from the rooftop pool between 5 and 7pm as the sun drops behind the city. It's also the least-crowded slot before the evening rush. Don't skip it.

tips.title: Request a soi-facing room
tips.body: Ask for an inner-facing or soi-facing room at check-in if you're a light sleeper. Road-facing rooms catch BTS and traffic noise that the inner rooms largely avoid.

tips.title: Buffet breakfast is worth adding
tips.body: At ฿209 per adult, the breakfast buffet (Thai, Chinese, American) is genuinely good value if you eat a proper morning meal. Add it when you book or request it at check-in.

tips.title: W District for evening out
tips.body: W District — the popular outdoor bar, street food and lifestyle compound in the On Nut–Phra Khanong area — is about a 5-minute Grab ride away. A great option for a relaxed evening without heading all the way to Thonglor.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Quarter Onnut by UHG

faq.q: Where is The Quarter Onnut by UHG, and how far is it from BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 1 Sukhumvit Soi 58, Phra Khanong Tai, Bangkok 10260, inside the Sukhumvit Hills mixed-use development. It's approximately 760 metres (10-min walk) to BTS On Nut and a similar distance to BTS Bang Chak in the other direction.

faq.q: What are the room rates at The Quarter Onnut by UHG?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately ฿1,200/night for a Superior King Room (21–27 sqm) in low season. The Deluxe Room (35 sqm) starts around ฿1,800/night. During high season (Nov–Feb) or Motor Expo period, prices rise — book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate.

faq.q: Does The Quarter Onnut by UHG have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has an outdoor rooftop swimming pool with Bangkok skyline views. It's consistently cited as the best feature of the property by guests. There's also a fitness centre with modern equipment on the same rooftop level.

faq.q: Is The Quarter Onnut by UHG good for families?
faq.a: Yes. The hotel offers a Family Suite with two bedrooms, suitable for families or groups of 3–4. The location in Phra Khanong is quieter than central Sukhumvit, and the BTS access makes getting around manageable even with children.

faq.q: What is there to do near The Quarter Onnut by UHG?
faq.a: The On Nut–Phra Khanong neighbourhood has a lot to offer: W District (popular outdoor bar and street food complex), Habito Mall, Summer Hill (indie cafes and brunch), Big C supermarket, and plenty of local street food and restaurants. BTS On Nut connects you to Siam (for shopping) in under 20 minutes.
